nodes.summary: `Λₙ` is measurable with respect to `σ(X₁, …, Xₙ)`, so the SPRT decides after `n` observations from those observations only (Lai 2001, §2, equation (2.1)).
nodes.title: The cumulative log-likelihood ratio is adapted

nodes.summary: `ADD(τ) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} πₙ Eₙ[(τ - n)⁺]` with `πₙ = ρ (1 - ρ)^{n-1}` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equations (7) and (11)); the delay is computed in `ℕ∞` (truncated subtraction, `⊤ - n = ⊤`).
nodes.title: Average detection delay under a geometric prior

nodes.summary: For `ν ≥ 1`, the observations are independent, `X₁, …, X_{ν-1}` have law `P₀` and `X_ν, X_{ν+1}, …` have law `P₁` (so `X_ν` is the first post-change observation, the convention of Lai 2001, §3, and of Veeravalli–Banerjee, §III-A). For `ν = 0` every observation has law `P₁`.
nodes.title: Law of the observations with a change point

nodes.summary: Let `P₀ ≠ P₁` be mutually absolutely continuous, let `c > 0`, and let `γ` be the mean time to false alarm `E_∞[N_c]` of the CUSUM alarm `N_c = inf {n ≥ 1 : W_n ≥ c}`. Then `N_c` minimises Lorden's worst-case delay `sup_ν ess sup E_ν[(T - ν + 1)⁺ | X₁, …, X_{ν-1}]` among all stopping times `T` with `E_∞[T] ≥ γ` (Moustakides 1986, as stated in Lai 2001, §3, p. 316; Lorden 1971 had proved asymptotic optimality as…
nodes.title: Moustakides' theorem: optimality of CUSUM under Lorden's criterion

nodes.summary: For a threshold `c`, `N_c = inf {n ≥ 1 : W_n ≥ c}` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equation (43)); `⊤` if no alarm is raised.
nodes.title: CUSUM alarm time

nodes.summary: `PFA(τ) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} πₙ Pₙ(τ < n)` with `πₙ = ρ (1 - ρ)^{n-1}` and `Pₙ = changePointLaw P₀ P₁ n` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equations (8) and (11)).
nodes.title: Probability of false alarm under a geometric prior

nodes.summary: If `P₁ ≪ P₀` and the event `A` depends only on the observations `X₁, …, Xₙ`, then `P₁^ℕ(A) = ∫_A ∏_{i<n} (dP₁/dP₀)(Xᵢ) dP₀^ℕ`: the likelihood ratio `Rₙ` is the density of `P₁^ℕ` with respect to `P₀^ℕ` on `σ(X₁, …, Xₙ)`. This is the change of measure behind Wald's inequalities (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, *Sequential probability ratio test*, equation (a2)).
nodes.title: Likelihood-ratio change of measure on the first `n` observations

nodes.summary: The SPRT stopping time is a stopping time of the observations, possibly infinite (Lai 2001, §2, equation (2.1)).
nodes.title: The SPRT stopping time is a stopping time

nodes.summary: `Λₙ = ∑_{i=1}^{n} log (dP₁/dP₀)(Xᵢ)`, the logarithm of the likelihood ratio `Rₙ` of the first `n` observations (`Λ₀ = 0`); each term is Mathlib's log-likelihood ratio `llr P₁ P₀ = log (dP₁/dP₀)`, with the Radon–Nikodym derivative read in `ℝ`.
nodes.title: Cumulative log-likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: For a stopping time `T`, `sup_{ν ≥ 1} ess sup E_ν[(T - ν + 1)⁺ | X₁, …, X_{ν-1}]` (Lorden's convention, as in Lai 2001, §3), written without conditional expectations: for a nonnegative variable `Y` and a `σ`-algebra `𝓕`, `ess sup E[Y | 𝓕] = sup {E[Y; F] / P(F) : F ∈ 𝓕, P(F) > 0}`.
nodes.title: Lorden's worst-case detection delay

nodes.summary: On the coordinate space `ℕ → X`, the `σ`-algebra at time `n` is generated by the coordinates `0, …, n - 1`, that is by the observations `X₁, …, Xₙ`; at time `0` it is trivial.
nodes.title: Filtration of the first `n` observations

nodes.summary: Closed form of the CUSUM statistic (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equations (44)–(45)): `W_n = max_{0 ≤ j ≤ n} ∑_{i=j}^{n-1} log L(ω i)`, the largest log-likelihood ratio of a final segment of the first `n` observations (the empty segment contributes `0`).
nodes.title: Closed form of the CUSUM statistic

nodes.summary: `W₀ = 0` and `W_{n+1} = max (W_n + log L(X_{n+1})) 0`, where `log L = log (dP₁/dP₀)` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equation (45)).
nodes.title: Page's CUSUM statistic

nodes.summary: If `P₁ ≪ P₀` are probability measures on `X` and `ι` is finite, the product law `P₁^ι` has density `x ↦ ∏ i, (dP₁/dP₀)(x i)` with respect to `P₀^ι`: the likelihood ratio of `|ι|` independent observations, as in the integrals of Wald's inequalities (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, *Sequential probability ratio test*, equations (a1)–(a2)).
nodes.title: Density of a finite product of absolutely continuous laws

nodes.summary: Under a geometric prior `P(Γ = n) = ρ (1 - ρ)^{n-1}` on the change point, `p₀ = 0` and `p_{n+1} = p̃ₙ L(X_{n+1}) / (p̃ₙ L(X_{n+1}) + 1 - p̃ₙ)` with `p̃ₙ = pₙ + (1 - pₙ) ρ` and `L = dP₁/dP₀` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equations (12)–(14)).
nodes.title: Shiryaev's posterior probability of a change

nodes.summary: Let `P₀ ≠ P₁` be mutually absolutely continuous with `D(P₁ ‖ P₀) < ∞`, let the change point have the geometric prior `ρ (1 - ρ)^{n-1}` with `0 < ρ < 1`, and let `0 < A < 1` be a threshold whose Shiryaev rule `τ_S = inf {n ≥ 1 : pₙ ≥ A}` has false-alarm probability exactly `α`. Then `τ_S` minimises the average detection delay `E[(τ - Γ)⁺]` among all stopping times `τ` with false-alarm probability `P(τ < Γ) ≤ α`…
nodes.title: Shiryaev's theorem: Bayesian optimality of the Shiryaev rule

nodes.summary: For a threshold `A`, `τ_S = inf {n ≥ 1 : pₙ ≥ A}` (Veeravalli–Banerjee, equation (15)).
nodes.title: Shiryaev's alarm time

nodes.summary: For the SPRT with log-boundaries `a` and `b`, `e^b P₀(accept P₁) ≤ P₁(accept P₁)`: the second line of Wald's inequalities, `1 - β = ∫_{λ_N ≥ B} λ_N dP₀ ≥ B α` (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, *Sequential probability ratio test*, equation (a2), whose upper boundary `B` is `e^b` here). With the first inequality it gives Wald's approximations `e^b ≈ (1 - β)/α` and `e^a ≈ β/(1 - α)`, which are equalities when the…
nodes.title: Wald's inequality on the acceptance of the alternative

nodes.summary: `{N < ∞ and Λ_N ≥ b}`.
nodes.title: Event that the SPRT stops and accepts `P₁`

nodes.summary: For the SPRT with log-boundaries `a` and `b`, `P₁(accept P₀) ≤ e^a P₀(accept P₀)`, where both events require the test to stop. This is the first line of Wald's inequalities, `β = ∫_{λ_N ≤ A} λ_N dP₀ ≤ A (1 - α)` (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, *Sequential probability ratio test*, equation (a2), whose lower boundary `A` is `e^a` here); `1 - α` equals `P₀(accept P₀)` when the SPRT stops `P₀`-almost surely. The source…
nodes.title: Wald's inequality on the acceptance of the null hypothesis

nodes.summary: `{N < ∞ and Λ_N ≤ a}`.
nodes.title: Event that the SPRT stops and accepts `P₀`

nodes.summary: With log-boundaries `a < 0 < b`, the SPRT stops at `N = inf {n ≥ 1 : Λₙ ≤ a or Λₙ ≥ b}` (`⊤` if this never happens) and accepts `P₁` when `Λ_N ≥ b`, `P₀` when `Λ_N ≤ a` (Lai 2001, equation (2.1), with `A = exp b` and `B = exp a`).
nodes.title: Wald's sequential probability ratio test

nodes.summary: Let `P₀ ≠ P₁` be mutually absolutely continuous and consider the SPRT with log-boundaries `a < 0 < b`. Let `(T, D)` be any test: a stopping time `T` of the observations with finite expected value under both hypotheses, and a rejection region `D` for `P₀` in the stopped `σ`-algebra, whose error probabilities `P₀(D)` and `P₁(Dᶜ)` do not exceed those of the SPRT. nodes.title: Wald–Wolfowitz theorem: optimality of the SPRT
